transcript: Meeting header: 2026-04-03 15:30 PST | Duration: 60m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood Solutions), Emma Li (NovaEdge PM), Daniel Park (NovaEdge Integration), Sofia Ortega (NovaEdge Marketplace)

Summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for joint solution (hosted + private deployment), and integration work to enable listing in NovaEdge marketplace. Discussed certification timeline, networking/KMS constraints, benchmarking plan, and next steps.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, I'll kick us off. Priya and Marco are on the call to cover the technical bits. Emma, thanks for coordinating on NovaEdge side.
[00:18] Emma: Yep thanks Alex, excited to sync. We want to make sure the marketplace listing and joint-solution doc are aligned before our partner enablement window in mid-April.

[00:28] Priya: Quick agenda - listing metadata and assets, reference arch (VPC/control plane + on-prem package), integration points (auth, billing hooks), and then benching plan for latency and cost numbers. Sound good?
[00:42] Daniel: Sounds good, we also need to confirm packaging - whether you provide a helm chart or an OCI image for the on-prem deployment.

[00:52] Marco: For Private deployments we offer both - a customer-managed control plane with an on-prem agent and a helm chart for k8s installs. The helm chart is maintained in our partner repo, so we can prod a sample chart.

[01:10] Sofia: From a marketplace perspective we have acceptance criteria: SOC2 report, SSO (SAML/OIDC) integration, logos/marketing copy, and a reference arch diagram. Also a smoke test run to validate the listed offering before go-live.
[01:30] Alex: Great. On SOC2 we already have the report - we'll attach the summary. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC; Priya can map the SSO endpoints to NovaEdge's expected flows.

[01:45] Priya: One note - our Private package supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM). For marketplace listing we need to call out that customers can bring their own keys and that logs are available for audits.
[02:05] Daniel: Our security team will want the exact encryption-at-rest details; also the network requirements. Do you require outbound connectivity from the customer network for telemetry/updates?

[02:17] Priya: The on-prem agent needs egress for update checks and telemetry, but we also have an air-gapped flow where updates are pushed via an offline bundle. We'll add both flows to the reference arch.
[02:34] Emma: Good - list both. For marketplace certification we need the articulate steps and typical time-to-cert. Sofia, what's the window?

[02:45] Sofia: Generally 7-10 business days once we have all artifacts and a verified test run. If there are security exceptions it can take longer. Ideally we get everything by next Monday for a mid-April listing.
[03:02] Alex: We'll aim to send the listing draft and artifacts by Monday. Marco - can you provide the sample helm chart and a minimal smoke test container image?

[03:16] Marco: Yep I can drop links. I'll attach a README that includes ports, env variables, and a sample manifests set. Note: some of our docs sometimes call KV cache "KV cash" - sorry transcription, but the runtime uses KV cache for long-context serving.

[03:38] Daniel: On the integration side we need to know whether Redwood exposes any billing webhooks for marketplace billing reconciliation, or if you expect NovaEdge to manage billing and call Redwood APIs.

[03:49] Alex: We have a marketplace billing integration pattern: partner can either integrate via our metered billing API or we can support a reseller model. For NovaEdge marketplace, recommended is a billing webhook for usage reports plus a reconciliation CSV export. We'll provide the spec.
[04:10] Emma: Okay we'll evaluate which model fits our marketplace policies. Another question - model variants. Can customers pin to specific model versions if they buy via the marketplace?

[04:20] Priya: Yes - customers can pin models and versions. We also support automated fallbacks to lighter quantized variants for cheaper tiers. We'll document supported model variants and latency expectations in the listing.
[04:36] Sofia: Please include the typical P50/P95 latency numbers per model variant - that's a must for marketplace listing pages.
[04:46] Alex: We'll run a small benchmark matrix and include P50/P95 for the common payload sizes. Priya - can you own the benchmark plan?

[04:53] Priya: Yep I'll spin up a matrix: small prompt (32 tokens), medium (128), long (512); run hosted vs dedicated vs private on equivalent hardware (A100 or NovaEdge-specified instance) and capture latency/cost.

[05:10] Daniel: For private deployments we have different instance types; I'd like to run the bench on a 4xA100 node we have in our lab. Is there tooling we can reuse from Redwood for consistent load generation?
[05:22] Marco: We'll share our bench harness (loadgen) and a script that reproduces tokenization/seq length distributions. It uses continuous batching to emulate production patterns.

[05:35] Emma: Great. On the reference arch diagram, we want a version for both NovaEdge-hosted marketplace offering (hosted by Redwood) and a co-managed offering where NovaEdge sells and Redwood operates, and also an on-prem variant.

[05:50] Priya: We'll prepare three panels in the diagram: Hosted API path (Redwood runtime in region), Dedicated/reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated pool with tenant isolation), and Private (VPC + on-prem agent + KMS). Each panel will call out networking ports, SSO flows, and data residency guarantees.

[06:12] Sofia: For the marketplace listing requirements you need to include a short customer-facing description, a longer technical overview, integration docs link, and pricing tiers. We'll provide a template for the listing fields.

[06:25] Alex: We'll use your template. Also want to call out deviation: some of our internal product names sometimes get transcribed - e.g., Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Dedicate - apologies in docs. We'll be consistent in the listing.
[06:40] Daniel: Network question - our security needs to know if the on-prem agent accepts inbound control-plane connections or only outbound. Which is it?
[06:50] Priya: Agent is outbound only by default for security. We do support a tunnel-based inbound control plane for special cases but it's opt-in and documented under "airgap/tunnel" flow.

[07:05] Emma: Excellent. A few nitty-gritty items: NovaEdge requires a marketplace tile that includes a link to a quickstart, a 1-page reference arch PDF, and a contact for support with SLAs. Can Redwood provide a support email and escalation path?
[07:20] Alex: Yes we'll provide a partner support alias and a chart of SLAs for hosted/dedicated/private. For enterprise SLA we can include 99.9% uptime and a priority escalation path.
[07:33] Sofia: On dependencies, please indicate if the offering requires specific cloud regions or GPUs only available in certain regions - that'll affect listing availability.

[07:43] Marco: We'll list supported regions and recommended GPU SKUs per deployment profile. Also note quantization: some models can run on T4/RTX-class hardware but with tradeoffs in throughput/latency.
[07:58] Daniel: About compliance docs: we need a pointer to your SOC2 scope and data retention policy. Also any third-party subprocessors.
[08:08] Alex: We'll attach SOC2 PDF, data retention overview, and subprocessors list. We'll redact anything that shouldn't be public.

[08:20] Emma: Perfect. Can we talk about timeline? If Redwood delivers listing assets by 2026-04-05 and NovaEdge completes review by 2026-04-07, certification should finish by 2026-04-16 and tentative listing week of 2026-04-20 - does that align?
[08:40] Sofia: Yes that timeline is reasonable assuming no major security exceptions.

[08:48] Priya: One more technical caveat - when we publish benchmark numbers for the marketplace, we should include the exact test config: sequence length distribution, batch sizes, and tokenization. Otherwise numbers get misused.
[09:02] Marco: Agreed. We'll include an appendix with the bench config and the raw logs for auditors if needed.
[09:12] Daniel: Regarding joint solution co-marketing, are you open to a joint reference architecture blog + webinar once the listing goes live?
[09:21] Alex: Absolutely. We typically do a press/blog + webinar with the top partner. Let's tentatively schedule that for late April / early May.
[09:33] Emma: Sounds good. A quick practical ask - Sofia, can you share the marketplace metadata template right after this call?
[09:40] Sofia: I'll drop it in the partner channel and link it in the follow-up email.

[09:48] Alex: Cool. Recap of action items: Priya reference arch draft by 4/10, Marco sample helm chart and smoke test, Daniel share KMS + CI constraints by 4/8, Sofia confirm acceptance criteria by 4/6, Alex send one-pager and pricing sketch by 4/5.
[10:05] Emma: We'll review the artifacts as they come and aim for the certification window. Thanks everyone - any other open questions?
[10:15] Daniel: One tiny thing: nonce/key rotation details - who rotates keys in the co-managed flow?
[10:21] Priya: In co-managed flow, customer controls KMS and rotates keys; Redwood supports automatic key rollover if the customer allows a key alias swap - we'll document exact steps.
[10:34] Alex: Great. If no more questions we'll end on that and send the follow-up with attachments and links.
[10:42] Emma: Thanks all, bye.

Post-call notes: Links shared during call - (1) partner-helm-sample repo (link to be attached), (2) bench harness script (link), (3) SOC2 summary (attachment). These will be included in the follow-up email.
Explicit next steps (repeat): Redwood to share marketplace listing draft + attachments by 2026-04-05; NovaEdge to provide assets and review; schedule benching week of 2026-04-13.
End of transcript.
